summary: Round-1 finding CR-1 applied: `from datetime import datetime, timezone` hoisted to top-of-file imports block; the local import inside the except block removed. Round-1 findings CR-2 / CR-3 / CR-4 are non-blocking observations (CR-2 deferred as scope creep, CR-3 already documented, CR-4 strength). The follow-up commit (fd6f1ed) also adds the outage_state.record_outage_event + admin-ping dispatch to the ClaudeOutageError branch; this aligns with the task-summary contract from the calling user message. State-machine update is wrapped in defensive try/except so the degraded-mode publish is never blocked by a state-write failure — correct ordering of priorities: re-raise still happens regardless.
strengths: Imports cleanly hoisted with no remaining local datetime imports.

Outage-state update path has correct error-handling layering: outer try captures state-write failures, inner per-ping try captures admin-notify failures. Each layer uses sanitize_error_message for redaction parity with the rest of the module.
outage_signal pattern keeps the re-raise contract intact — even if record_outage_event AND send_admin_notification both fail, the publish completes and ClaudeOutageError still propagates to job().
